facts.title: Vardavar
facts.text: On this day, generous splashes of water drench passersby and loved ones: a game children call djrotsi.

facts.title: The worship of Astghik
facts.text: The festival was tied to Astghik, goddess of water, beauty, love and fertility, and to the goddess Anahit.

facts.title: August 11
facts.text: He set the Transfiguration of Christ on the 1st of Navasard, the first day of the Armenian calendar.

facts.title: 98 days after Easter
facts.text: Linked to the Paschal cycle, the feast falls between June 28 and August 1, after a week of fasting.

facts.title: The memory of Noah
facts.text: From the ark on Mount Masis, Noah told his descendants to sprinkle water on one another and release doves.

facts.title: Vard, the rose
facts.text: Popular tradition sees in it the union of vard, rose, and var, burning or flaming.

facts.title: Since 2014
facts.text: The Federation of Youth Clubs of Armenia has organized the Vardavar International Festival there.

ytTitle: Vardavar: The Great Armenian Festival of Waters and Light
ytLead: Tied to the pre-Christian worship of Astghik, goddess of water, Vardavar became the Feast of the Transfiguration of the Armenian Apostolic Church. People splash one another with water, and it is inscribed on the list of Armenia's intangible cultural heritage.
